Readers are cautioned that these forward-looking statements are only predictions and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and assumptions that are difficult to predict, including those under “Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors,” and elsewhere herein. Therefore, actual results may differ materially and adversely from those expressed in any forward-looking statements. We undertake no obligation to revise or update any forward-looking statements for any reason. OVERVIEW Cisco designs and sells a broad range of technologies including hardware, software, and artificial intelligence (AI) powered digital infrastructure to power, help secure, and draw insights from the Internet. We are incorporating AI into our product portfolios across networking, security, collaboration and observability, as well as integrating our products more tightly together into a platform. We are simplifying how our technology is delivered, managed and optimized and helping customers maximize the business value of their technology investments. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Set forth below and elsewhere in this report and in other documents we file with the SEC are descriptions of the risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this report. Risks Related to our Business and Industry Our operations can be difficult to predict because our results of operations may fluctuate in future periods. Our results of operations have been in the past, and will continue to be, subject to quarterly and annual fluctuations as a result of numerous factors, some of which may contribute to more pronounced fluctuations in an uncertain global economic environment. Consequently, our results of operations are not a reliable indicator of future results. These factors include: • Customer patterns, such as fluctuating demand for our products and services, especially with respect to service providers and cloud customers; the timing, size, and mix of orders from customers; and changes in sales and implementation cycles for our products and reduced visibility into our customers’ spending plans and associated revenue • Our ability to maintain appropriate inventory levels and purchase commitments and manage manufacturing and customer lead times • Price and product competition in the communications and networking industries, which can change rapidly due to technological innovation and different business models from various geographic regions • Industry trends such as consolidation among our competitors and our customers, and the introduction and market acceptance of new technologies, products and technology standards, and our success in these new and evolving markets and with emerging technologies, including AI • Variations in sales channels, product costs, or mix of products sold (e.g., hardware and software sales, including mix of cloud-based and on-premise software sales) • Fluctuations in our gross margins, and the factors that contribute to such fluctuations • The ability of our direct sale customers, channel partners, contract manufacturers and suppliers to obtain financing, to fund capital expenditures, or withstand financial problems • Actual events, circumstances, outcomes, and amounts differing from judgments, assumptions, and estimates used in determining the values of certain assets (including the amounts of related valuation allowances), liabilities, and other items reflected in our Consolidated Financial Statements • How well we execute on our strategy and operating plans and the impact of changes in our business model that could result in significant restructuring charges • Our ability to achieve targeted cost reductions and anticipated benefits from our investments • Changes in tax laws or accounting rules, or interpretations thereof Any of these factors, or others discussed in this report, could materially harm our business, results of operations, or financial condition. Our results of operations may be negatively impacted by unfavorable economic and market conditions and the uncertain geopolitical environment. Our responsibility is to express opinions on the Company’s consolidated financial statements and on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audits. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin expanded year over year and sits comfortably above the sector median, reflecting pricing discipline and a richer software and subscription mix across networking, security and observability. This earnings power underpins cash generation through the cycle.

Free cash flow comfortably covers dividends and buybacks combined, and operating cash flow covers capital expenditure plus dividends with headroom. Internal funding therefore supports both the shareholder return programme and modest deleveraging without new borrowing.

key_risks.text: Results are disclosed as subject to pronounced quarterly and annual fluctuation from customer order timing, inventory and purchase commitments, and product mix shifts including cloud and service provider demand. Such volatility could compress margins and cash flow faster than the current profile implies.

Gross leverage sits above the sector median and net leverage on a cash-and-investments basis also exceeds the peer median, so the balance sheet carries less relative cushion than close competitors. Refinancing of near-term maturities adds execution dependence on continued market access.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved year over year and remains strong in absolute terms, though it trails the sector median. Operating income covers gross interest expense many times over, leaving ample room for rate resets on refinanced borrowings.

Free cash flow to debt is substantial but declined year over year and is modestly below the sector median, while operating cash flow to debt also softened. Debt service nonetheless remains comfortably funded from recurring cash generation rather than asset sales.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, with leverage well inside the next risk-band boundary and cash flow coverage far above its threshold. Our judgement is that the issuer retains substantial capacity to absorb earnings decline or incremental debt before the profile weakens.

Liquidity is the main structural blemish: the current ratio is below one and far under the sector median, with near-term debt maturities and distributions competing for cash. We view refinancing risk as manageable given cash generation, but working capital discipline warrants monitoring.

credit_strengths.text: 營業利潤率按年擴張，並穩居行業中位數之上，反映定價紀律，以及網絡、安全和可觀測性業務中更豐富的軟件與訂閱組合。此盈利能力支撐整個週期的現金生成。
自由現金流足以覆蓋股息與回購的總和，而經營現金流覆蓋資本開支加股息後仍有餘裕。因此，內部資金可同時支持股東回報計劃及溫和去槓桿，而無需新增借貸。

key_risks.text: 業績披露顯示，受到客戶訂單時機、庫存及採購承諾，以及包括雲端和服務供應商需求在內的產品組合轉變影響，季度及年度波動顯著。此類波動可能以快於當前狀況所暗示的速度壓縮利潤率和現金流。
總槓桿高於行業中位數，而按現金及投資計算的淨槓桿亦超過同業中位數，因此資產負債表相對緩衝少於密切競爭對手。短期到期債務的再融資增加了對持續市場準入的執行依賴。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年改善，絕對水平仍然強勁，儘管低於行業中位數。營業利潤覆蓋總利息支出的倍數甚高，為再融資借款的利率重設留有充裕空間。
自由現金流對債務比率可觀，但按年下降，並略低於行業中位數，而經營現金流對債務比率亦有所轉弱。儘管如此，債務償付仍可從經常性現金生成中獲得充裕資金，而非依賴資產出售。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，槓桿遠低於下一個風險區間邊界，而現金流覆蓋率遠高於其門檻。我們的判斷是，發行人在狀況轉弱之前，仍保有大量能力吸收盈利下降或增量債務。
流動性是主要結構性瑕疵：流動比率低於一，且遠低於行業中位數，短期到期債務與分派爭奪現金。鑑於現金生成能力，我們認為再融資風險可控，但營運資金紀律值得監察。
